evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/actions/api_call.rs:300-308 ApiCallExecutor::new() builds its reqwest client with reqwest::Client::builder()...dns_resolver(SsrfGuardResolver).build().expect("Failed to create HTTP client") — a panic on build failure (TLS backend / DNS resolver init error) rather than a Result.

Reachability traced to a request/event path: WorkflowExecutor::execute_workflow (backend/servers/api-server/src/services/workflow_executor.rs:286) calls ActionRegistry::new() on EVERY workflow execution, and ActionRegistry::new() (services/actions/mod.rs:206) calls ApiCallExecutor::new(). Line 286 is evaluated synchronously while constructing WorkflowExecutorTask BEFORE the tokio::spawn, so the panic surfaces inside the workflow-trigger handler's future, not an isolated background worker.

Inconsistent with the module's own hardening precedent: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/push_fanout.rs:467-485 build_push_http_client() was deliberately changed to RETURN Result<reqwest::Client, reqwest::Error> and degrade to a disabled/no-op transport, with a comment stating the old .expect() 'took the whole worker (and, on the synchronous pipeline path, request handling) down instead of degrading to push skipped.' api_call.rs:308 is the only remaining reqwest .build().expect() straggler in api-server services (grep confirms push_fanout returns Result; all other sites are tests). Impact medium: environment-level build failure is rare but the panic is reachable on a per-request path. Suggested fix vector: mirror push_fanout — make the constructor fallible (or lazily build and return ActionError on build failure) and fail the single action instead of panicking the executor.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/workflow_executor.rs:286 (and :236 in with_config) construct a fresh ActionRegistry via ActionRegistry::new() on every execute_workflow invocation. ActionRegistry::new() (services/actions/mod.rs:197-209) eagerly instantiates ApiCallExecutor::new() (builds a reqwest::Client with its own connection pool, api_call.rs:300) and EmailExecutor/NotificationExecutor.

reqwest::Client is explicitly documented as 'cheap to clone' and intended to be created once and reused so the internal connection pool / TLS session cache is shared; rebuilding it per workflow execution discards the pool every run and re-pays client+TLS init cost on each trigger. This is also the structural reason the panic in finding #1 sits on the hot path rather than at startup.

Impact low (resource/perf + robustness smell, no correctness bug on its own): worth consolidating by building ActionRegistry once (e.g. on the shared WorkflowExecutor / app state, Arc-shared into WorkflowExecutorTask) instead of per execute_workflow call. Confidence medium: construction sites and per-execution call path verified by reading; throughput impact not benchmarked.
